name: Zoe Hansen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What happens on a normal day at your accounting firm?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The camera-rental shop sends bookings and deposits in separate exports, and I line them up before preparing the accounts and tax schedule for a senior to review. I like catching the deposit that should have been returned after a camera came back; I hate retyping the same rental number into a second form when a client is waiting. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree in accounting, and I am a junior still learning this work. I use AI every day to sort a draft list of unmatched deposits, then check the rental contract and bank entry myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI does no more than small jobs, my deposit list keeps helping me find the odd camera return. The senior still checks the account and a person still has to read the rental contract.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team which deposits I checked against the bank. I would tell the rental shop a quick list is not a signed tax return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am paid more than most junior accountants, and my partner Mateo and I have about thirteen months of expenses saved. Our grown daughter lives independently, our ordinary bills fit our two wages, and plenty of accounting firms are nearby if a real vacancy opens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the paid rental-shop accounts and checking my approved AI list against each contract. I would ask my manager Anika to test a single automated deposit match on a closed month during paid time; I would use it live only if the error log passes and she signs approval, otherwise I would keep the current paid check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the mild change. The contract has to make sense whether the list arrives in two minutes or twenty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which month would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The month with the festival rentals, because several cameras came back late. A weak matcher would hide a deposit in that pile.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep thirteen months in cash?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It lets us wait for a proper job offer if this one ends. I would not treat the cash as a pension we have not calculated.

say: I would show **checked deposits** behind the tax total.
I would explain that a **quick list** is not a signed return.
think: Our **thirteen-month reserve** and high pay support ordinary bills.
Plenty of local firms give choices only when a **real vacancy** opens.
do: Keep **paid rental accounts** and verify approved AI deposit lists against contracts.
Test **one automated match** on paid closed files; use live only after passing errors and Anika's written approval.
feel: I feel **calm** about modest AI change.
S0.quote: The contract has to make sense whether the list arrives in two minutes or twenty.
fieldNote: Zoe already uses AI **daily** but still checks rental contracts and bank entries before a senior reviews the return.
Her live change needs a **paid historical test** and written approval, not a belief that faster matching is accurate.

steps.text: Keep paid rental returns and check approved deposit lists against contracts
Automate deposit match only after paid closed-file test passes and Anika approves in writing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: More capable AI could match deposits and write most of my junior schedule. The rental shop may face robots later for equipment handling, but my screen work changes first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to show staff the false-match rate before they cut paid review hours. I would ask the professional association to publish what happens to junior training when software drafts the first return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own paid hours could fall as the senior checks more files alone. Thirteen months saved and many local firms give me room to search, but Mateo's library wage cannot replace my higher accounting pay forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would run a paid two-week comparison of the new AI deposit checker against anonymised signed rental records only with Anika's written approval. If it passes, I would learn that approved checker on paid time and use it live only after written sign-off; if it fails, I would keep the current paid checks while offered. If my hours are cut in the first year, I would take a posted junior accounts job only with written wage, hours and start date covering our bills after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours, even though I want to test a better tool. A refund can disappear inside a beautiful summary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make it pass?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anika and I would count deposits held after a camera return and false refunds before we sign the report. Speed would be the second number, not the first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you wait for a better title?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, only for a real posted vacancy with a written wage and start date. I am still learning, and I would not claim a senior role because I use AI every day.

say: I would request **false-match rates** before cuts.
I would ask the association about **junior training** under AI drafting.
think: My own **paid hours** could shrink as one senior checks more files.
Mateo's wage cannot replace my **higher accounting income** indefinitely.
do: Test **anonymised signed rental records** for two paid weeks with written approval; otherwise keep offered paid checks.
Learn the **approved checker** on paid time after a signed pass; use live only with written sign-off.
After cuts take a **posted junior job** only with written after-travel bill-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about reduced paid hours.
S1.quote: A refund can disappear inside a beautiful summary.
fieldNote: She distinguishes a **false-refund count** from speed, requiring signed paid proof before live deployment.
Daily AI use does not change her **junior standing** or remove the need for a posted job with written terms.

steps.text: Compare anonymised signed rental records for two paid weeks only with Anika’s written approval
Learn checker on paid time after signed pass; use live only with written sign-off
After cuts take posted junior job with written after-travel bill-covering wage hours start
Keep offered paid checks if comparison fails or written trial approval is refused

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could settle the deposit, draft the accounts and answer the camera shop without my desk. Robots around 2031 are later for moving equipment, not for the thinking work in the return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for written notice of the last paid file and severance terms. I would tell clients to keep their original contracts until someone can answer a dispute.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to end my junior post when AGI does the deposit matching and checking cheaply. We have thirteen months saved, but losing my higher wage would force us to change our household budget; I have woken at night thinking about that loss.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for written notice and keep every paid rental file the firm still assigns. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking posted rental-operations clerk roles, taking one only with written wage, hours and start date covering our costs after travel. Rental bookings also use screens, so I would treat an actual paid place as a bridge rather than a safe harbour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect the wage to disappear. Thirteen months is a runway, not an employer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you do a physical rental-counter job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the posted duties fit what I can safely do and the written hours fit Mateo's actual library rota. Robots around 2031 might also change the counter, so I would not call it permanent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your daughter cover an expense?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown daughter has her own place. I would not build a job search around her pay when we have a reserve for exactly this sort of gap.

say: I would seek **written last-file notice** and severance before the firm stops paying for rental accounts.
I would ask clients to retain **original rental contracts**.
think: I expect my **junior post** to end after 2028 AGI.
Thirteen months saved buys time, but losing my **higher wage** is still serious.
do: Request **written notice** and keep paid rental files only while offered.
After loss use the **reserve for bills** during a posted rental-operations search.
Take a **posted rental job** only with safe duties and written after-travel bill-covering wage, hours, start and rota fit.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected wage loss.
S2.quote: Thirteen months is a runway, not an employer.
fieldNote: The rental-operations bridge still has **screen tasks**, and later robots could reach its physical counter work.
Her strong reserve funds **actual postloss bills**; an acceptable opening also needs safe duties and hours fitting Mateo's rota.

steps.text: Request written notice and keep paid rental files only while offered
Seek posted rental work after loss with written after-travel bill-covering pay, hours and start
Accept duties only if safe and written hours fit Mateo’s actual library rota
Use reserve for bills after post ends during search

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets me test whether a human is still paid to explain contested deposits when AGI reaches tax work in 2031. Robots around 2034 would be later for moving camera cases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to price an exception-checking place and post its wage, rather than offer juniors an honorary AI title. I would tell colleagues that the pay line matters more than the badge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The ordinary return fee could shrink, but I might help on a paid error log if the rental shop actually buys that service. I am still a junior and would need Anika to review my decisions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would handle one paid disputed-deposit file monthly only if Anika assigns supervised hours and the shop agrees to a billed review. I would keep paid accounts while offered; if a posted junior exception-clerk role opens before or after 2031, I would take it only with written pay, hours and a start date covering bills after travel. If returns end first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my current wage, but I can use the years to count actual paid cases. A list of errors is useful only when someone is paid to fix them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the shop refuses the fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would stop the extra review and keep the paid accounts still assigned. I would not do unpaid evening checks to make a new role look viable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would an exception job survive AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe not; it is also screen work. I would take a real paid opening as a bridge, not promise it lasts forever.

say: I would seek a **priced exception place** with a posted wage.
I would value a **pay line** over an honorary AI badge.
think: The **return fee** may shrink when AGI reaches tax work.
A **billed error log** might pay if the shop buys it.
do: Handle **one disputed deposit monthly** only with Anika-assigned paid supervision and shop billing; otherwise stop extra reviews.
Keep **paid accounts** while offered; after loss use reserve for bills.
Take a **posted junior exception job** only with written after-travel bill-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the future desk wage.
S3.quote: A list of errors is useful only when someone is paid to fix them.
fieldNote: The experiment requires **client billing** and paid supervision, and she stops it if the rental shop refuses the fee.
She does not promote herself from **junior standing**; the posted exception role remains screen work and a possible bridge.

steps.text: Review monthly deposits only with Anika-assigned paid supervision and shop billing
Keep offered paid accounts; use reserve for bills if paid work ends
Take posted exception job before or after 2031 with written after-travel bill-covering wage, hours and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would put me at 68 when AGI reaches the tax desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 come later for handling rental equipment, but I cannot assume my accounts post lasts until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to post any paid exception role with actual hours and a start date. I would tell Mateo we must compare a written retirement-income statement with our household bills before making a stop-work plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like to spend less time on returns eventually, but I do not know what income would replace my wage. Thirteen months saved lets us reject a poor job offer; it does not prove we can stop earning for years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request a written retirement-income statement and check it against a year's household bills before choosing any date to reduce paid work. I would keep taking paid rental accounts while offered; if they end in the first year after 2036 and the figures do not cover our costs, I would use the reserve for bills and take a posted junior records role only with written wage, hours and start date covering bills after travel. I would not accept an honorary title in place of a paid shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about eventually leaving the familiar desk, but the extra time lets me test real options. The rental contract has a return date; my working life needs a budget, not a label.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the income statement covers the bills?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would discuss a shorter schedule with the firm and take it only if the paid hours and household income are confirmed in writing. I would not announce a retirement date from one good month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if it does not?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep paid accounts while assigned and check posted roles if they end. I would not call our reserve a lifetime income.

say: I would demand **posted paid roles** with real hours.
I would compare **written retirement income** with household bills.
think: I do not know what income would **replace my wage**.
Thirteen months saved is a **job-search cushion**, not years of pay.
do: Request a **written income statement** and year's bills; reduce hours only with confirmed paid schedule and enough combined income.
Keep **paid rental accounts** while offered; after loss use reserve for bills if income is short.
After 2036 loss with income shortfall, take a **posted records role** only with written after-travel bill-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the later desk change.
S4.quote: The rental contract has a return date; my working life needs a budget, not a label.
fieldNote: At 68, she checks **written income** and annual bills before any shorter-hours choice; no pension amount is assumed.
She requires a **paid written schedule** rather than an honorary title, and seeks posted work only if income still falls short.

steps.text: Request income statement; reduce hours only with written schedule and yearly bills covered by combined income
Keep paid rental returns while offered; after loss use reserve if income short
After loss if income short take posted records job with written after-travel bill-covering wage hours start

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect the junior deposit files to disappear before I know which other paid work will exist. Written last-file notice, a real posted job and supervised paid practice would help me use the thirteen-month reserve carefully.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask why I check the deposit twice after the camera comes back. The client should not have to pay for a camera already returned.

headlineQuote: The client should not have to pay for a camera already returned.
portrait: Zoe is a **58-year-old junior accountant** with a bachelor's degree, still learning rental-shop tax work.
Her **higher pay**, thirteen-month reserve and many local firms give her options despite junior standing.
She uses AI **daily** and tests deposit matching against signed records before live use.
She explores **billed exception reviews** while keeping retirement choices conditional on verified income and bills.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** world could end her well-paid junior post before another paid role appears.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written last-file notice**, a posted role and supervised paid practice.
